expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | { status: "trialing"; trialEndDate: Date } | { status: "active"; renewalDate: Date } | ...

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states '**`subscription.trialEndDate` is a compile error** unless the type system has narrowed to `status: "trialing"`'

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Shows assertNever function with default case, and states 'Enforce `@typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check` in CI'

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Shows branded types only for RetryCount (a value), not for subscription/customer IDs: 'This prevents passing arbitrary numbers where only valid counts belong' — optional section, wrong category

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function or state machine shown; only shows exhaustive handling of existing states

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: 'Now:' section explicitly names prevented misuses: '**`subscription.trialEndDate` is a compile error**', '**Adding a state breaks the build**', '**The database schema can enforce it**'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated unions; bag-of-optionals only mentioned as what to avoid
